newsitem.title: USA: Keith Crain named chairman of Crain Communications.
newsitem.headline: Keith Crain named chairman of Crain Communications.

text.p: Crain Communications Inc. said it named Keith Crain chairman of the family-run company that publishes 30 business, trade and consumer titles, including Advertising Age, Automotive News and weekly business papers in Chicago, Cleveland, Detroit and New York.
Rance Crain, president of the company and editor in chief of Advertising Age, keeps his current titles, sources inside the company said.

With the changes, Keith Crain, formerly vice chairman, becomes the third chairman in the company's 81-year history, filling the position left vacant when his mother, Gertrude Crain, retired last May. Mrs. Crain, who retained the title of chairman emeritus, became chairman in 1974 following the death of her husband and company founder G.D. Crain Jr.
Mrs. Crain died in July, leaving some speculation about which of her sons would succeed her.
Crain Communications was founded in 1916. In addition to its publications, Crain operates two radio stations and has 16 offices worldwide.
